audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $348.255 million FY2025 acquisition cash outflow; recurring acquisition requirement unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring acquisition spending needed to produce the modeled 4%-7% growth would reduce future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The cash used in investing activities primarily consisted of $348.3 million of acquisition-related consideration related mainly to the Irwin and LiquidityBook transactions, $108.8 million of capital expenditures mainly driven by the capitalization of internal-use software development costs, partially offset by $58.2 million in proceeds from our investments in mutual funds.
audit_findings.explanation: The spending is filed and large relative to the $584.7 million anchor, but it is not demonstrated to be recurring or necessary for the modeled growth. FY2025 organic revenue grew 4.4%, while Organic ASV grew 5.7% at August 2025 and 7.1% at May 2026, indicating that at least some modeled growth may be achievable organically. The record does not isolate organic OE or establish a normalized acquisition requirement.
audit_findings.action: Construct an acquisition-free OE history, reconcile acquired versus organic earnings, and rerun the base and bull cases with any demonstrated normalized acquisition cash requirement deducted from OE.

audit_findings.title: The after-tax anchor may capitalize an unusually low tax rate
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 rate 17.2% versus 18.4% for nine months FY2026; applying 18.4% to the FY2025 pre-tax equivalent would reduce anchor OE by approximately $8.5 million and base value by approximately $3.31 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A sustainable tax rate above the anchor-year rate reduces after-tax OE in every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: This was primarily attributable to excess tax benefits from stock-based compensation, a lower U.S. tax impact of foreign earnings, research and development ("R&D") tax credits and a foreign derived intangible income ("FDII") tax deduction, partially offset by our state income taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The 17.2% rate includes stock-compensation benefits and other tax advantages of differing durability. The subsequent 18.4% rate demonstrates some normalization, but that observed change would reduce base value only about 1.4%. The record does not establish the sustainable rate or separate recurring geographic and R&D benefits from volatile stock-compensation and law-dependent benefits, so the full materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate FY2025 OE using a normalized cash tax rate that excludes discrete stock-compensation benefits and separately tests durable R&D, FDII and foreign-income benefits; rerun all scenarios at the supported rate.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earn-outs appear to be omitted claims ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.953 million remaining at May 31, 2026, equal to approximately $0.26 per diluted share and 0.11% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid earn-out not captured in OE should be deducted as a claim in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: These liabilities reflect the present value of potential future payments that are contingent upon the achievement of certain specified milestones and are valued using a scenario-based method.
audit_findings.explanation: The $24.126 million August 2025 liability had declined to $9.953 million by May 2026, while $16.176 million of deferred acquisition consideration had already been paid and therefore had already reduced the latest cash position. Deducting the entire remaining liability would lower each scenario by only about $0.26 per share and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the $9.953 million balance is not already captured elsewhere, then deduct it from the bridge for completeness; no broader rerun is needed.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may retain a nonrecurring divestiture gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.238 million pre-tax and $17.205 million after tax; if fully retained, approximately $255.5 million or $6.74 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time gain included in anchor OE is grown and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in Net income and Diluted EPS for fiscal 2025, compared with fiscal 2024, was primarily driven by higher operating income and a gain from the divestiture of a business.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the gain survives in the $584.7 million anchor is unresolved, but its maximum identified effect is computable. Removing the filed $17.205 million after-tax gain would reduce the base estimate from $236.92 to approximately $230.18 per share, about 2.8%, still well below the $301.96 market price and leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged.
audit_findings.action: Trace the anchor calculation; if included, remove the $17.205 million after-tax gain and rerun the scenarios while treating any disposed recurring operations consistently.

audit_findings.title: Existing uncertain-tax claims may be absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $46.497 million of total current and non-current taxes payable at May 31, 2026, equal to approximately $1.23 per share and 0.52% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any historical tax exposure not already reflected in OE or working capital is an incremental claim to deduct in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, there were $ 38.5 million, $ 29.1 million and $ 19.1 million of unrecognized tax benefits that, if recognized, would affect the annual effective tax rate.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing reports $5.182 million of current taxes payable and $41.315 million of non-current taxes payable. Even the conservative assumption that the entire $46.497 million is incremental would reduce base value by only about $1.23 per share. The uncertain-tax component may be smaller because the balances also can contain ordinary tax liabilities, so this cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the May 2026 tax-payable accounts to unrecognized tax benefits, accrued interest and ordinary taxes; deduct only the portion not already captured in OE or normalized working capital.

audit_findings.title: The anchor relies on revenue systems subject to an unresolved material weakness
audit_findings.mechanism: A misstatement in revenue, receivables or deferred revenue could alter net income and working-capital adjustments used to calculate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Our Principal Executive Officer and Principal Financial Officer have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of the end of the annual period covered by this report due to a material weakness in internal control over financial reporting.
audit_findings.explanation: The control deficiency is demonstrated and remained unresolved at May 31, 2026, but no valuation-input error is demonstrated. Management reported no identified misstatement, performed additional procedures, and the FY2025 financial statements received an unqualified audit opinion. Because the weakness creates a reasonable possibility of an undetected material misstatement, the effect on OE cannot be quantified or dismissed from the present record.
audit_findings.action: Review the FY2026 10-K for completed remediation and auditor testing; reconcile FY2025 revenue, receivables, deferred revenue and OE working-capital inputs to the audited statements and rerun only if a quantified correction is identified.
